_note: Seed dataset curated from public NASA descriptions of ISS combustion investigations. Condition ranges and years are APPROXIMATE (verified=false) and must be checked against NASA PSI (https://psi.ssl.nasa.gov) once the official challenge resources are released. Scores 0-3 in safety_pillars / partial_gravity are editorial judgements used by the ranking model.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.sample_geometry: flat sheets, rods/cylinders and spheres, a few cm in size
investigations.objective: Measure how solid materials ignite, spread flame and extinguish in microgravity as a function of forced flow speed and oxygen concentration.
key_findings: Many solids burned steadily in microgravity at low flow speeds typical of spacecraft ventilation.
Near-limit flames are weak and blue; they can survive at oxygen levels close to or below normal-gravity limits when low forced flow is present.
Nitrogen dilution and flow reduction extinguished flames, giving data for suppression strategy.
earth_applications: fire spread models for vehicles and buildings

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
investigations.sample_geometry: thin and thick flat samples, cylinders, spheres
investigations.objective: Extend BASS to more materials and lower oxygen levels to find microgravity flammability limits (limiting oxygen vs. flow speed).
key_findings: Mapped flammability boundaries (minimum O2 vs flow speed) for thin and thick solids in microgravity.
At low ventilation speeds some materials remained flammable at lower O2 than in normal-gravity upward-burning tests, suggesting ground tests may not always be conservative.
Data underpins efforts to add microgravity correction to material selection tests.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration I
investigations.sample_geometry: large sheet, about 0.4 m x 0.94 m
investigations.objective: First large-scale fire in a spacecraft: measure flame spread and growth over a large fabric sample in concurrent flow.
measurements: O2/CO2 and pressure in the vehicle
key_findings: Demonstrated a large flame in a real spacecraft volume for the first time.
Flame spread and growth reached a limited size rather than growing without bound under the tested flow.
Provided scale-up data to validate fire spread models built from small glovebox tests.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration II
investigations.sample_geometry: nine smaller samples, about 5 cm x 30 cm
investigations.objective: Test ignition and flammability of a range of spacecraft cabin materials at different flow speeds in a real vehicle.
key_findings: Compared which common cabin materials sustain flame and which self-extinguish in microgravity.
Results feed directly into material selection for crewed vehicles.
earth_applications: material selection for aircraft and transit interiors

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration III
investigations.sample_geometry: large sheet, about 0.4 m x 0.94 m
investigations.objective: Repeat the large-scale burn with different flow and ignition conditions to test repeatability and fire growth.
key_findings: Large-scale flame spread data complementary to Saffire-I.
Showed the effect of flow configuration on fire growth in a vehicle-sized volume.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigations.sample_geometry: small samples heated (overheated, not flaming) on a wire/heater
investigations.objective: Measure the size distribution of smoke particles from overheated spacecraft materials in microgravity to improve smoke detector design.
key_findings: Smoke particle size distributions from overheated materials differ from normal gravity, partly because particles stay near the source and grow longer.
Some smokes would be poorly detected by the original ISS detectors; results inform next-generation detectors.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
investigations.sample_geometry: small heated samples
investigations.objective: Reflight of SAME with improved hardware and more conditions to characterize smoke particles for detector requirements.
key_findings: Expanded smoke particle database for spacecraft materials.
Supports detector specifications for future exploration vehicles.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.sample_geometry: ambient cabin air
investigations.objective: Test whether a commercial ultrafine particle counter (also used in SAME) works in microgravity, for later dust/smoke monitoring.
key_findings: The particle counter worked in microgravity, enabling its use in smoke studies such as SAME.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test 2
investigations.sample_geometry: ambient cabin air
investigations.objective: Follow-up measurements of cabin aerosol background, which sets the noise floor for smoke detection.
key_findings: Characterized background aerosol levels that smoke detectors must distinguish from fire smoke.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.sample_geometry: free-floating or tethered droplets, about 1-5 mm diameter
investigations.objective: Find the concentration of gaseous suppressants (CO2, He) needed to extinguish burning fuel droplets in microgravity.
key_findings: Measured extinction limits of droplet flames diluted with CO2 and helium; guides suppressant concentrations in spacecraft.
Discovered that large heptane droplets keep burning after visible flame extinction via low-temperature 'cool flame' chemistry.
Radiative heat loss is a key extinction mechanism for large flames in microgravity.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
investigations.sample_geometry: single droplets and droplet pairs/arrays
investigations.objective: Study burning rate, sooting and extinction of multi-component and multi-droplet fuels, including droplets in slow convective flow.
key_findings: Quantified how fuel mixtures and neighboring droplets change burning rate and extinction.
Provides data for spray-fire and fuel-leak fire models.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation (droplets)
investigations.sample_geometry: free droplets, about 2-5 mm
investigations.objective: Study low-temperature 'cool flame' burning of fuel droplets that was first seen in FLEX.
key_findings: Cool flames can persist at temperatures far below normal flames, producing partial-oxidation products.
A fire that looks extinguished may still be reacting - relevant for re-ignition and toxic products.
earth_applications: engine knock and low-temperature combustion models

investigations.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
investigations.sample_geometry: gas jet burners, sub-mm to ~1 mm nozzles, in co-flowing air
investigations.objective: Measure the smoke point (flame length at which soot escapes) of gas-jet flames in microgravity.
key_findings: Microgravity flames are longer and sootier than normal-gravity flames of the same fuel flow.
Smoke points differ from ground values, important for smoke production and radiation in fires.

investigations.name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.sample_geometry: gas jet burners in co-flow
investigations.objective: Study lift-off and blow-out of jet flames, i.e. how a flame detaches and stabilizes away from the burner.
key_findings: Lift-off heights and stability limits differ in microgravity, testing flame stabilization theory without buoyancy.

investigations.name: ACME - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
investigations.sample_geometry: round coflow burner
investigations.objective: Provide benchmark data on soot and flame structure of laminar coflow flames to validate computational combustion models.
key_findings: Benchmark flames for validating CFD soot and flame models used in fire prediction.

investigations.name: ACME - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame)
investigations.sample_geometry: spherical porous burner
investigations.objective: Study spherical diffusion flames and their extinction to test combustion kinetics and radiation models.
key_findings: Radiative extinction of large spherical flames tests the limits of flame existence without buoyancy.

investigations.name: ACME - Flame Design
investigations.sample_geometry: spherical porous burner (normal and inverse flames)
investigations.objective: Learn how flame structure (normal vs. inverse, O2 enrichment) controls soot formation, to design soot-free flames.
key_findings: Oxygen-enriched and inverse flames can be made soot-free, showing how O2 level changes flame chemistry and smoke.

investigations.name: ACME - Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.sample_geometry: flat porous burner that emulates a burning solid/liquid surface
investigations.objective: Emulate burning of condensed materials with gaseous fuels to find flammability limits as a function of material properties (heat of combustion and gasification) in still atmospheres.
key_findings: Links material properties to whether a material can sustain a flame in quiescent microgravity.
Tested elevated O2 and reduced pressure relevant to exploration atmospheres.

investigations.name: ACME - Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (E-FIELD Flames)
investigations.sample_geometry: coflow burner with electrode mesh
investigations.objective: Use electric fields acting on flame ions ('ionic wind') to control flames - mimicking buoyancy and partial gravity.
key_findings: Electric fields reshape flames similar to how buoyancy does, offering a ground-free proxy for partial gravity.
The only PSI combustion data set that mimics partial-gravity effects.

investigations.name: ACME - Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)
investigations.sample_geometry: spherical porous burner, inside-out (O2 from burner into fuel/N2 chamber)
investigations.objective: Produce and study cool diffusion flames of gaseous fuels, including at very high oxygen concentrations.
variables: O2 fraction of burner flow (up to ~85%)
key_findings: Highest-oxygen microgravity flames in PSI - the closest data to spacesuit and high-O2 habitat conditions.
Gaseous cool flames exist and transition to/from hot flames depending on O2 and flow.
